newsitem.title: CHINA: China mulls ferry, rail links for Hainan island.
newsitem.headline: China mulls ferry, rail links for Hainan island.

text.p: China is looking to build a rail and ferry link to connect the island province of Hainan with the mainland at a cost of 1.76 billion yuan ($212 million), the official Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

Xinhua said the ferry would link the port of Qinzhou in Guangxi with Yangpu, an economic development zone, in Hainan. A rail link would extend between Yangpu and Sanya on the southern part of the island.
A feasibility study on the link, which would be largely for freight, has been completed and domestic and overseas business interests have discussed the project with authorities.
The potential investors were not identified and no timetable for the project was given.
Hainan is also moving ahead slowly with a rail and ferry link between the island and the mainland province of Guangdong.

That project, approved by authorities in 1993, includes a rail line from Maoming in Guangdong to the port of Haian. A ferry would connect Haian and Haikou in Hainan, and another railway link would be built between Haikou and the city of Chahe, also on Hainan.
More than 100 million yuan has so far been invested in the five-billion yuan project, which is being jointly undertaken by Guangdong and Hainan as well as the Ministry of Railways.
Construction of the Hainan-Guangdong rail and ferry link has been slow due to a shortage of funds, Xinhua said.
